model.title: Department of Energy Nuclear Transparency Act

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: The following analysis is based on draft bill text that was made available by the House of Representatives and may differ from the bill text as introduced.
Department of Energy Nuclear Transparency Act

This bill directs the Department of Energy (DOE) to report actions related to its authorization of DOE nuclear facilities and other related DOE actions on a public website within 72 hours of those authorizations or actions occurring.

Specifically, DOE must post information about agreements to authorize nuclear facilities that fall under Hazard Category 1, 2, or 3. Hazard categories are based on the radioactive material inventories of the facilities and the potential consequences to the public, workers, and the environment. Hazard Category 1 represents the highest potential consequence.
DOE must also post a summary of any actions it took to alter a directive or safety standard relating to such facilities.

Further, DOE must post any preliminary documented safety analysis or documented safety analysis that it issues for such facilities. A preliminary documented safety analysis means documentation prepared in connection with the design and construction of a new Hazard Category 1, 2, or 3 DOE nuclear facility or a major modification to such nuclear facility already in existence that provides a reasonable basis for the preliminary conclusion that the nuclear facility can be operated safely through the consideration of certain factors. A documented safety analysis means a documented analysis of the extent to which a nuclear facility can be operated safely with respect to workers, the public, and the environment.
DOE must also issue an annual report detailing any activities it took to authorize such DOE nuclear facilities during the previous year.

The Department of Energy Nuclear Transparency Act would require the Department of Energy to publicly post information about certain nuclear facility decisions on a public website within 72 hours of those decisions or actions taking place.

The posted information would cover agreements to authorize nuclear facilities in Hazard Category 1, 2, or 3. These categories are based on how much radioactive material a facility holds and how much harm it could cause to the public, workers, and the environment, with Hazard Category 1 representing the greatest potential harm.
The Department would also have to post a summary of any steps it took to change a directive or safety standard that applies to these facilities.

In addition, the Department would be required to post any preliminary documented safety analysis or documented safety analysis it issues for these facilities. A preliminary documented safety analysis is prepared during the design and construction of a new facility, or a major change to an existing one, and gives a reasonable basis for concluding preliminarily that the facility can be operated safely. A documented safety analysis is a written review of how safely a facility can operate with respect to workers, the public, and the environment.
Finally, the Department would have to issue an annual report describing what it did to authorize these nuclear facilities during the previous year.
